name: SSD1309 2.42" OLED display 128x64 (SPI)
description: 2.42-inch monochrome 128x64 OLED driven by a Solomon Systech SSD1309 controller on 4-wire SPI (write only: SCL = clock, SDA = data in, DC = command/data, CS active low, RES active-low reset). SSD1306-style command set but no internal charge pump: the module's boost converter makes the panel supply and an XC6206 regulator makes the 3.3 V logic supply. Runs on 3.3-5 V. Sold as: LCDwiki / QDtech MSP242X 2.42inch SPI OLED Module (MSP242W white / MSP242B blue / MSP242Y yellow, 7-pin header GND, VCC, SCL, SDA, RES, DC, CS), the common 7-pin SPI version of the 2.42" SSD1309 module (also sold under HiLetgo, Teyleten Robot, DWEII and similar names).
eli5: A big, bright little screen that shows text and pictures as glowing dots, talking over a fast 4-wire link.

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: SPI data in (SSD1309 D1/SDIN); connect to MOSI

pins.name: DC
pins.description: Data/command select: low = command, high = data

supplierQuery: 2.42 inch OLED SSD1309 128x64 SPI 7 pin module
buildNotes: Header order is GND, VCC, SCL, SDA, RES, DC, CS. GND is pin 1, so check the silkscreen before you power it.
SCL and SDA are the SPI clock and SPI data (MOSI) on this board, not I2C. There is no MISO: the SSD1309 serial interface is write only.
The board ships in 4-wire SPI mode (only R5 fitted). Fitting R4 and R9 instead switches it to I2C; leave them alone for this part.
CS must be driven (R8, which would tie CS to GND, is not fitted by default).
The SSD1309 logic runs at 3.3 V from the module's XC6206 regulator and the signal pins go straight to the chip, so 3.3 V logic (ESP32, Pico, Raspberry Pi) is the safe choice.
Keep SCLK at or below 10 MHz (datasheet clock cycle time 100 ns minimum); the driver uses 8 MHz, SPI mode 0.
About 52 mA maximum per the module specification; mostly dark screens draw much less.
The SSD1309 has no charge pump. Code ported from the SSD1306 that sends 8Dh is unneeded; this driver leaves it out.

driver.code:
# SSD1309 128x64 OLED on 4-wire SPI (e.g. LCDwiki / QDtech MSP242X 2.42" SPI&IIC module), MicroPython driver.
# Written from the Solomon Systech SSD1309 datasheet Rev 1.1 and the module maker's init sequence.
# 4-wire SPI (datasheet 8.1.3): write only, MSB first, data sampled on SCLK rising edge,
# D/C# low = command byte, high = GDDRAM data; CS# active low. SCLK cycle >= 100 ns (<= 10 MHz).
# The SSD1309 has no internal charge pump (no 8Dh command): the module's boost converter makes VCC.
import framebuf
import time


class SSD1309_SPI(framebuf.FrameBuffer):
    def __init__(self, width, height, spi, dc, res, cs, baudrate=8_000_000):
        self.width = width
        self.height = height
        self.spi = spi
        self.dc = dc
        self.res = res
        self.cs = cs
        self.rate = baudrate
        self.pages = height // 8
        self.buffer = bytearray(self.pages * width)
        super().__init__(self.buffer, width, height, framebuf.MONO_VLSB)
        dc.init(dc.OUT, value=0)
        cs.init(cs.OUT, value=1)
        res.init(res.OUT, value=1)
        # Power ON sequence (datasheet 8.8): after VDD is stable hold RES# low >= 3 us, then high.
        time.sleep_ms(1)
        res(0)
        time.sleep_ms(1)
        res(1)
        time.sleep_ms(1)
        self.init_display()

    def _write(self, dc, buf):
        self.spi.init(baudrate=self.rate, polarity=0, phase=0)
        self.cs(1)
        self.dc(dc)
        self.cs(0)
        self.spi.write(buf)
        self.cs(1)

    def cmd(self, *b):
        self._write(0, bytes(b))

    def init_display(self):
        self.cmd(0xAE)                    # display off
        self.cmd(0xFD, 0x12)              # command lock off (unlocked; reset state)
        self.cmd(0xD5, 0xA0)              # clock divide 1, oscillator setting 1010b (module maker's value)
        self.cmd(0xA8, self.height - 1)   # multiplex ratio
        self.cmd(0xD3, 0x00)              # display offset 0
        self.cmd(0x40)                    # start line 0
        self.cmd(0x20, 0x00)              # horizontal addressing mode
        self.cmd(0xA1)                    # column 127 -> SEG0 (panel mounted mirrored)
        self.cmd(0xC8)                    # COM scan COM[N-1] -> COM0
        self.cmd(0xDA, 0x12)              # alternative COM pin configuration
        self.cmd(0x81, 0xBF)              # contrast
        self.cmd(0xD9, 0xF1)              # pre-charge phase 1 = 1 DCLK, phase 2 = 15 DCLK
        self.cmd(0xDB, 0x34)              # VCOMH ~0.78 x VCC (reset value)
        self.cmd(0xA4)                    # display follows RAM
        self.cmd(0xA6)                    # normal (not inverted)
        self.fill(0)
        self.show()
        self.cmd(0xAF)                    # display on (SEG/COM on after 100 ms)

    def poweroff(self):
        self.cmd(0xAE)

    def poweron(self):
        self.cmd(0xAF)

    def contrast(self, c):
        self.cmd(0x81, c & 0xFF)

    def invert(self, on):
        self.cmd(0xA7 if on else 0xA6)

    def show(self):
        self.cmd(0x21, 0, self.width - 1)   # column range
        self.cmd(0x22, 0, self.pages - 1)   # page range
        self._write(1, self.buffer)

example.code:
from machine import Pin, SPI
import time
from ssd1309_spi import SSD1309_SPI

spi = SPI(1, baudrate=8000000, polarity=0, phase=0, sck=Pin({SCL}), mosi=Pin({SDA}))
oled = SSD1309_SPI(128, 64, spi, dc=Pin({DC}), res=Pin({RES}), cs=Pin({CS}))
oled.fill(0)
oled.text('Hello 2.42 SPI', 0, 0)
oled.text('SSD1309 SPI ok', 0, 16)
oled.show()
while True:
    time.sleep(1)
